items.title: Bounty auto earner: one click delivery packager for the six proven report services
items.body:
Owner directive 2026-10-23 evening: build BOTH earning programs toward the 1 dollar per minute target. This task is the bounty lane half, repo work only.

Goal: cut the delivery time for a won 10 USD report job to under 10 minutes of compute, start to checked deliverable, so a delivered job earns at or above 1 dollar per minute while it runs.

Build, inside this repo only:
1. A delivery packager that takes a job spec (service name, subject, buyer ask) for the six proven services (recall, FMCSA carrier, federal litigation, Form D, nonprofit, federal awards) and assembles the report from the existing fetchers in tools/ and the templates in workstream D, with every claim carrying its source and retrieval time.
2. A verification pass that fails the package if any claim lacks a source, if counts do not match the fetcher output, or if the deliverable hash is not recorded.
3. A timing log per delivery run, so the coordinator can report minutes per job and dollars per minute honestly.
4. One filled example per service, built from public data only, checked the same way.

Rules: repo work only. No bids, no submissions, no accounts, no keys, no wallet or payment handling in this repo; bidding and delivery on Synmerco, NEAR, and the other lanes stay with the coordinator and the existing lane jobs under their standing approvals. No pricing changes in this task; pricing is the owner decision and is tracked on issue 147.

Acceptance: packager runs on all six services, verification pass demonstrably fails a deliberately unsourced example, timing log exists, and the PR states the measured minutes per example job.

items.title: Private security bounties: automatic GitHub receipt, AI triage, owner-decided awards
items.body:
## Summary

Private reports now reach a verified case without a maintainer link check, get a private AI triage proposal, and only the owner's award decision reserves money. The case pages show each person only what they need.

- **Receipt.** A signed-in reporter starts a private report. Slop first checks live that GitHub private vulnerability reporting is on, then hands off to GitHub's own private form. Slop then reads the repository's private vulnerability reports through a read-only advisory token and records the case under the GitHub author, at GitHub's `created_at`. The reporter must reconcile before submitting again: an open submission is returned again, and "unavailable" never means "no report". A maintainer import picks up reports sent on GitHub directly. Old unverified links are settled against GitHub. The manual claim, verify, reject and hand-typed record flows are removed.
- **Automatic private analysis.** It proposes a summary, severity, possible loss of funds, duplicates (only earlier cases it was given), a root-cause key and remediation. D1 keeps only the proposal and the advisory digest. Report text never reaches D1, logs or Slopbot. The provider must be configured explicitly; without it the analysis is recorded as unavailable and can be re-run.
- **Discretionary award.** Severity and loss are guidance, not eligibility. The owner chooses no award or an amount. Approving an amount reserves exactly that gross atomically if verified funds cover it; otherwise nothing is written (`insufficient_funds`). One award per root cause. Related-party awards still need an independent reviewer. Payment uses the reserved amount with the exact 75/25 integer split, the separate private ledger and the existing escrow adapters. Report, award, payment and disclosure states stay separate.
- **UI.**
  - Reporter: receipt, owner response and payout.
  - Owner: AI summary plus request-information, decide, award and remediation.
  - Everyone: one next step derived from case state.
  - Triager and disclosure tools fold away until relevant; appeal and dispute tools appear only when allowed.

Why Slop does not submit for the reporter: GitHub's `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories/reports` accepts a GitHub App user access token. Using it needs the reporter's user token at submission time, the app installed with advisory write on every program repository, and Slop holding the report text. The identity Worker never keeps user tokens, and an installation token would submit as the app rather than the reporter. So the reporter submits on GitHub and Slop verifies the receipt automatically. Adopting the user-token route is listed below as an owner decision.

## Audit findings addressed

- **10: Private reporting is still manual.** Automatic receipt verification, submission ID with reconcile-before-retry, private analysis, maintainer notice on receipt, direct GitHub submission as recovery.
- **11: Eligibility and reservation contradict discretion.** Owner chooses none or an amount; approval reserves atomically when funds exist; severity is not an entitlement or a bar.
- **12: Reduce routine case chores.** Simplified reporter and owner views, derived next actions, 75/25 split, private access checks and private ledger kept.

These were re-verified against `6a93bf1a` first; none had been fixed upstream.

## PRD references

- PRD section 8, "Report and decide privately" and "Pay a private award".
- PRD section 10 rows: Intake, Eligibility and fix, Access and decisions (two authorities), Capacity, Amounts, Privacy.
- PRD section 7 user journey: Researcher.
- SEC-01 to SEC-18; MVP work package MVP-13.

## What changed

- `migrations/0061_security_automatic_intake.sql`:
  - New columns: `received_at_source`, `award_gross_minor`.
  - New tables: `security_submissions`, `security_case_analyses`.
  - Immutability triggers.
- `backend/security/advisories.ts`: read-only GitHub private report reader. It returns a complete list or "unavailable", never a partial answer.
- `backend/security/analysis.ts`: provider-backed private analysis with fixed endpoints, output validation and retry rules.
- `backend/security/handler.ts`:
  - Submission and import routes, receipt reconciliation, derived next steps.
  - `request-information` and `award` actions; analysis and funds shown in the owner view.
  - Funds-checked atomic reservation.
  - Removed: claim/record/verify-link/reject-link/triage/next-action/approve-award/reserve-award and earliest-receipt ordering. Historical event kinds stay readable.
- `functions/api/v1/[[path]].ts`: wires `SECURITY_ADVISORY_READ_TOKEN`, `SECURITY_ANALYSIS_PROFILE` and `SECURITY_ANALYSIS_API_KEY`. Unset means unavailable and fails closed.
- `src/SecurityBounty.tsx`: report starter, receipt confirmation, maintainer import, simplified case view, AI summary panel, award form with exact-split preview. Public terms now describe discretionary awards.
- Tests: rewritten `backend/security/handler.test.ts`, new `advisories.test.ts`, updated `payments.integration.ts`, `workers/notify/security.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/security-bounty.spec.ts`. The GitHub fixture and e2e runner gained synthetic private advisories behind a fixture token.
- `backend/security/README.md` updated.

## Tests

- `bun test backend/security workers/notify/security.test.ts`: 24 pass.
- `bun backend/security/payments.integration.ts` (local anvil, synthetic): pass.
- `SLOP_E2E_LANE=registry node scripts/run-e2e.mjs tests/e2e/security-bounty.spec.ts`: 8/8 pass (2 tests × 4 viewports) on local Pages, local D1 and the loopback GitHub fixture. Needed a gitignored `public/data/leaderboard.json` prepared from `tests/fixtures` with `scripts/prepare-pr-ledger.ts`.
- `bun x tsc -b`: pass.
- `bun run lint:check`: pass (warnings only; the ones in changed files existed before).
- `bun run test:notify` and the `backend/notifications` + `backend/security` part of `verify:code`: pass.
- `bun run test:scripts`: 261 pass, 3 fail. The 3 are timeouts in `scripts/vetting-api.test.ts` while the machine was heavily loaded; they pass 12/12 with `--timeout 120000`.

## Not verified

- No real GitHub API, model provider, chain, email or deployed environment. The token and provider configuration are human-provisioned and not set up.
- No real LLM call for the analysis; it is tested with an injected analyzer.
- No full `bun run verify`, and no manual keyboard, 200% zoom or video evidence beyond the automated browser spec (axe on several screens; 200% zoom on the disclosure and settlement screens).
- A local test is not a deployment. The private bounty rail still needs a reviewed vault and explicit activation.

## Open owner decisions

1. **Funds measure for reservations.** Implemented and fail-closed as published gross per finding × award count minus reservations, verified funding only. The alternative is the bounty vault's finalized free balance.
2. **Submitting for the reporter** via a GitHub App user access token.
3. **Analysis provider and model** allowed to read private report text, and its retention terms.
4. **Advisory read credential type.** A GitHub App installation token is preferred over a long-lived token.
5. **Separation of duties.** Please confirm that dropping the old "technical decider cannot approve or prepare payment" rule, following PRD section 10's two authorities, is intended.
6. **Awards without paid terms.** Awards remain limited to cases received while paid terms were open.

## Related issues

#910 (work package order 5). Context: #908.

---
Part of the parallel implementation of the October 22 Slop code/PRD audit (one draft PR per work package). Cross-package follow-ups are listed in the body.

Blacksite now supports local player listings, banked bid escrow, net buyout settlement, exact-instance protected delivery and anonymous local bounties paid by normal contested/open-zone deaths. Money, item ownership, delivery, Kestrel fees, market records and private audit commit through one commerce source. Schema 4 preserves bid/history snapshots, expiry and retirement refunds.

Public-terminal F9 services preserve E contract-board interactions and street M/O/C map/drone/chat. Market D bids, Esc/B leaves, and Y confirms a chosen transfer. Purchased goods collect free from market-tagged delivery; unsold returns restore inventory weight so cancellation cannot bypass apartment storage. Views and operator list responses are paged for accumulated history. S28/S29/S30 and S25 handoffs retain PR #38 and issue #56 decisions.

Validation:
- Full root pytest at f23120938ec42af75d8853337ef839dc5304218b: Linux/Python 3.12 1,449 passed; Windows/Python 3.12 1,448 passed, one skipped (last Windows gate green; detailed final log will be recorded).

- Native acceptance is NOT complete. Installed 0.0.19 through actual NetBBS 7.31 native stdio at 80x24 reaches public services and lists the physical starter pistol. That exposed missing advertised action metadata, now fixed and covered through the real client key model. A subsequent buyer route hit an unexpected chat prompt; its failed trace is retained and under investigation. The parallel 132x50 attempt timed out during cold door launch before gameplay.

Entity 2.6, architecture 15.2 and terminal UI 4 describe records, atomicity, access and bounded views. S23 uses actual commissioned Vatside contested geography; S25 retains actual Sink travel and real commerce/clinic acceptance, and S25/S26 retain human pacing gates. Grade/full-pool/bank fixtures are disclosed; no item, placement, reward or future-map fixture is used.

Preferred slice implementer: Sonnet. Actual implementer: Codex (GPT-6); automated Claude review supplies the review gate. Triage will fix credible caller/operator/security/data-loss impact and explain deferrals of theoretical correctness findings.

The one open team bounty today (*Gnars x Nouns Mini App*, 30 USDC) was on `/community/bounties` but not on `/`. - **Fix:** open Sopa bounties now join the hand. Bounties from team wallets (`POIDH_SOPA.teamIssuers`) lead it, newest first, with a **⌐◨-◨ GNARS TEAM** mark. Everything else, community Sopa bounties and poidh skate/surf, ranks by USD value, so a near-zero bounty from anyone sinks instead of taking the Legendary slot. The service's 60 s cache was cutting the homepage ISR from 5 min to 1 min (confirmed in `next build`); the homepage now passes its own 300 s. A new bounty can take up to 5 min to reach `/`; `/community/bounties` stays at 1 min. - `messages/{en,pt-br}/newhome.json`: team mark, Sopa card type, partial-failure notices; section copy now says "ETH or USDC". - `docs/integrations/poidh-sopa.md` + `docs/INDEX.md`: homepage ranking and how to add a team wallet. ## Tests - [x] `tsc`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` (1982 passed) - [x] Unit: `bounty-hand.test.ts` (ranking, totals, codes) - [x] Component: `BountiesSection.test.tsx` (24 cases, EN + PT-BR with real messages): team mark and order, stranger ranking, totals, USDC-only pool, no ETH price, each source failing alone, both failing, loading, empty, six-card cap. Mutation-checked: breaking the team flag or the totals gate fails it. - [x] E2E: `tests/e2e/home-bounties.spec.ts` on live data: team card raised and claiming on-site, poidh card claim on poidh.xyz, 320/375/768 px with no horizontal scroll, PT-BR copy, light/dark, no page or hydration errors - [x] `next build` + `next start`: e2e 18/18 (with `i18n.spec.ts`); `/`, `/pt-br`, `/community/bounties`, `sopa/0`, `sopa/1` and both APIs return 200 - [ ] Vercel preview (needs a SOPA team member to authorize the deploy) - [ ] Real check on a phone ## Not in this PR - Who counts as "team" is only the SOPA wallet so far. Other members' bounties show, but without the mark, until their wallets are added. - A partial Sopa read on the server can still deal the hand without Sopa cards and let them join after hydration. Rare, and the same as `/community/bounties` today. - Card backs show raw markdown headings (`## Goal`). Pre-existing for poidh cards too.

items.title: [Bounties] Fechar para votação e encerrar bounty pelo site
items.body:
Hoje, nas bounties da Sopa, quem cria a bounty só tem duas opções:

Pagar os vencedores na hora. O contrato permite fechar a bounty para votação, mas o site não mostra essa opção.
Encerrar a bounty. O botão fica no último card da lateral, que no celular aparece lá no fim da página. O texto diz "recuperar seus fundos", mas não explica como nem onde.
E quando alguém recebe um pagamento ou um reembolso, o dinheiro não cai direto na carteira: ele fica como saldo para sacar, e a página da bounty não mostra onde fazer esse saque.

Correção (PR #17): https://github.com/gnars-dao/gnars.com/pull/17

Na hora de escolher os vencedores, o criador escolhe entre Pagar agora e Fechar para votação. A votação dura 48 h, e enquanto ela acontece ninguém consegue enviar novos claims.
Aparece um novo card Gerenciar bounty logo abaixo da descrição, visível só para o criador, com o botão de encerrar.
O aviso de saque aparece na própria página da bounty.
Os textos em PT e EN explicam para onde vai o dinheiro e quem vota.

items.title: feat(bounty): implement payout-address indirection for anonymity-preserving claims (#238)
items.body:
## Summary

Implements anonymity-preserving payout-address indirection on `RefractBountyEscrow` so researchers can claim bounties without permanently linking their disclosure identity to their payout wallet on-chain.

Closes #238

---

## Changes

- **Commitment-Bound Disclosures & Adjudication (`bounty/src/lib.rs`)**:
  - `compute_commitment(preimage)`: computes `SHA-256(preimage)` for 32-byte secret preimages.
  - `submit_disclosure(submitter, report_hash, commitment)`: binds a vulnerability disclosure `report_hash` to a payout `commitment` instead of the submitter's funding address, rejecting duplicate reports and commitment reuse across reports (`BountyError::CommitmentAlreadyUsed`).
  - `award_commitment(caller, report_hash, commitment, amount)`: governance-gated entrypoint that adjudicates a report against its `commitment` and reserves `amount` in the `CommitmentAwardStatus::Awarded` state without exposing the destination wallet.
- **Front-Running-Resistant Payout Binding & Rotation (`bounty/src/lib.rs`)**:
  - `register_payout_address(owner, preimage, payout_address)`: requires `preimage` at registration to prevent front-running, stores `PayoutBindingRecord` in persistent storage with explicit TTL extension (`extend_ttl`) and bounded lifetime (`DEFAULT_BINDING_TTL_SECS`), and emits `p_reg`.
  - `rotate_payout_address(owner, preimage, new_payout_address)`: allows the binding owner to rotate the payout destination prior to claim, atomically revoking the previous payout address so two addresses can never claim the same award, and emits `p_rotate`.
- **Preimage-Verified Claim & Compromised-Address Freeze (`bounty/src/lib.rs`)**:
  - `claim_by_commitment(caller, preimage)`: verifies the preimage, checks binding ownership/TTL/freeze state, transitions the award from `Awarded` to `Claimed`, releases the reservation, transfers the reward to the bound `payout_address`, and emits `c_claim`.
  - `freeze_payout_address(caller, address, frozen)`: governance-gated entrypoint to freeze or unfreeze a compromised payout address without altering the awarded reward amount (allowing the binding owner to rotate to a clean address before claiming). By design, lost keys/preimages are an unrecoverable loss with no admin redirect override.
- **Documentation (`SECURITY.md`, `bounty/src/lib.rs`)**:
  - Documented the commitment registration, adjudication, rotation, freeze, claim, and lost-key semantics in both `SECURITY.md` and the crate-level rustdoc.
- **Unit Tests (`bounty/src/test.rs`)**:
  - `indirection_register_award_rotate_claim_happy_path`
  - `indirection_double_claim_rejected`
  - `indirection_commitment_reuse_rejected`
  - `indirection_claim_with_wrong_preimage_rejected`
  - `indirection_rotation_by_non_owner_rejected`
  - `indirection_binding_ttl_expiry_rejected`
  - `indirection_freeze_compromised_payout_address_preserves_reward_and_allows_rotation`

## Checklist
- [x] Zero `unwrap()`, `expect()`, or `panic!()` calls in non-test contract code
- [x] Persistent storage entries extended with explicit TTLs
- [x] `SECURITY.md` and crate documentation updated

items.title: Region 1 guided path T7: Theme tracking and refresher bounties
items.body:
Part of #24, the Region 1 guided-path spec. That issue has the sources, the order and what's deferred.

- **Blocked by:** T2 (#27), T6a (#25), T6b (#28).
- **Unblocks:** T8 (#33).

## Work

- **Save:** `themeStats: Record<tag, { misses: number; streak: number; lastMissAt: number }>`, where `lastMissAt` is `battlesFought` at the time of the miss.
- **Tag to warm-up table** (Region 1 content, next to T2 (#27)'s warm-ups):

  | Tag | Warm-up |
  | --- | --- |
  | `hangingPiece` | Trouble in the Reeds |
  | `defensiveMove` | Lanterns at Mossbridge |
  | `backRankMate` | Behind the Mud Wall |
  | `promotion` | The Pawn's Plunge |
  | `mateIn1` | None |

  A tag with no warm-up still gets refreshers, just without the "Warm up first" button. The Swap Meet also uses `hangingPiece`, and its mistakes count toward that tag.
- **Battle mistakes: one update per accepted result.** The result is recorded at once (`recordResult`, `Battle.ts`), but the review finishes later, gives up after 6 seconds, and is dropped if you leave or rewind. So:
  - The update happens when the result is accepted: for a win, when it's recorded; for a loss, when you choose Retry or Retreat, or leave (the same points that call `recordAcceptedLoss` in `src/flow.ts`).
  - It uses the review's result if it has finished, and the costliest mistake (`biggestMistake`, `src/game/review.ts`) counts a miss for the battle's own warm-up tag.
  - If the review hasn't finished (timed out, the engine is unavailable, or you left first), no mistake is recorded.
  - A rewind discards the result, so nothing is recorded for it. The next accepted result, if any, records once.
  - At most one update per battle played. A result accepted twice (for example a Retry, then leaving) still counts once.
- **Bounties:** a failed bounty counts a miss for its `theme` and resets `streak` to 0. A solved one adds 1 to `streak`.
- **Weakest theme:** among tags with a miss in the last 3 battles fought (`battlesFought - lastMissAt <= 3`) and `streak < 2`, pick the most recent miss. Ties go to the most misses, then curriculum order (`CURRICULUM_THEMES`). Two solves in a row drop a tag out.
- **Refresh** (`refreshBounties`, `src/game/economy.ts`): if a weakest theme exists, 1 of the 4 slots is an unused puzzle with that tag, marked "Refresher". If the tag has a warm-up, the slot gets a "Warm up first" button that opens it in replay mode, with no pay. If the tag has no unused puzzle left, try the next weakest; if none qualifies, all 4 slots work as today.
  - Refreshers pay like other bounties until playtests say otherwise (an open question in the decision log).
- **Tests, with a fixed `rng`:**
  - each rule above;
  - leaving before the review finishes records nothing;
  - rewinding a reviewed defeat records nothing;
  - Retry then leave records once;
  - a `mateIn1` refresher has no warm-up button;
  - an exhausted tag falls through to the next.

**Done when:** a theme you miss comes back as a refresher on the next refresh, drops off after two solves in a row, and discarded or unreviewed results never count.

## Checks

`npm run ci` before the PR. This ticket changes no battle positions or AI, so the engine playtests shouldn't rerun; if `npm run ci` decides they should, let them run.

## Work

Today only `mateIn1` and `hangingPiece` have display text. `THEME_TEXT` (`src/puzzles.ts:28`) defines nothing else, and `Puzzle.ts:107`, `Puzzle.ts:166` and `Town.ts:255` read `.name` and `.task` directly. So a puzzle with any other theme crashes, and `puzzleTheme`'s fallback calls anything that isn't mate in one a hanging piece.

- **`THEME_TEXT`:** add a name, task text and companion line for `defensiveMove`, `backRankMate` and `promotion`, plus any other tag a Region 1 warm-up uses.
- **`puzzleTheme`:** use `p.theme` when set (bounty pack files and T2 (#27)'s inline warm-up puzzles both set it). Otherwise take the first tag in `CURRICULUM_THEMES` order that the puzzle carries.

- `src/puzzles.ts` `THEMES` and `src/game/bounty.ts` `CURRICULUM_THEMES`: add the three tags.
- `scripts/build-puzzles.mjs`: add the three tags to Region 1's `themes`, run `npm run puzzles`, and commit `public/puzzles/region1/*.json` and `index.json`. Never commit `data/raw/`.
- **Tests:** for each Region 1 tag, a puzzle of that tag opens (name and task resolve) and plays through to solved; an unknown theme gets the fallback; ids are unique across packs.

**Done when:** bounties draw on all five tags, and a puzzle of each tag opens and can be solved.

items.body:
Closes #19 ## Summary - On Sopa bounties the creator could only **open and pay**. Gnars bounties are funded only by the team wallet, and in that case the winners picker showed nothing but "Pay", even though the contract accepts `submitWinnersForVote`. The creator now picks **Pay now** or **Close for vote**. - Ending a bounty (`cancelOpenBounty` / `cancelSoloBounty`) was the last card in the sidebar, at the very bottom of the page on phones. It moves into a new **Manage bounty** card under the description, visible only to the creator. - Payouts and refunds are credited to `pendingWithdrawals`, not transferred. The withdraw banner now also renders on the bounty page, so winners and a creator who ended a bounty can withdraw there. - Copy in EN and PT-BR now says where the money goes and who votes (contribution-weighted; Gnars NFTs don't count). Explainer for the team, with the same screenshots: https://claude.ai/artifact/48Yw7QqX62gvbodb5K4S8n ## Before / after Phone width (390 px), PT-BR. "Before" is `main`; "After" is this PR. **Picking winners** | Before | After | | :---: | :---: | | | | | Pay is the only path. | Pay now or Close for vote, each explained. | **Ending a bounty** | Before | After | | :---: | :---: | | | | | Button 3,462 px from the top. | Button 1,633 px from the top. | | | | | "Recover your funds", with no how or where. | Says the share comes back as a balance to withdraw on this page. |
320 px phone and desktop (EN)
Screens use bounty #1's real data rendered as still open, with the creator view forced on a local dev server. No transaction was sent. ## Contract behavior (simulated on Base mainnet before building) `eth_simulateV1` against PoidhSopa `0x31d0…F505`: - `submitWinnersForVote` from the issuer works on an open bounty with no outside contributor. - While a vote runs, `createClaim`, `joinOpenBounty` and `cancelOpenBounty` revert `VotingOngoing`. So "Close for vote" also closes the bounty to new claims. - `votingPeriod()` = 172800 s (48 h). After it, `resolveVote` from any address pays the winners (credited to `pendingWithdrawals`, net of the 2.5% fee). - `cancelOpenBounty` credits the issuer's share to `pendingWithdrawals(issuer, token)`; no transfer. ## Changes - `SopaWinnersPicker.tsx`: Pay now / Close for vote switch (toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`) on open bounties without outside contributors. Reads `votingPeriod` for the copy. Stacks below `sm`; claim rows fit 320 px. - `SopaBountyDetailView.tsx`: Manage bounty card (next step + end with confirm) replaces the sidebar cancel card; `SopaWithdrawalBanner` at the top of the page. - `messages/{en,pt-br}/bounties.json`: new strings in both locales, plus clearer existing ones. PT-BR now uses wallet / prêmio / criador / apurar votação consistently. - `docs/integrations/poidh-sopa.md`: vote lifecycle and where refunds land. `docs/i18n/tone-brief.md`: three new terms. ## Checks - `tsc`, `pnpm lint` (0 errors; the 20 warnings are pre-existing, none in these files), `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` (1951 passed). - Ran in the browser at 320 / 390 / 768 / 1280 px, light and dark, PT-BR and EN, touch and keyboard. - No conflict with #16 (both touch `bounties.json`; merge simulated clean). - `pnpm build` not run locally. - **Needs the team wallet (`0xA642…dFD68`) after deploy:** close a bounty for vote, resolve after 48 h, and withdraw.

items.title: Spec: Region 1 guided path (warm-ups, main path and branches, library, refresher bounties)
items.body:
Spec for revising Region 1 to the **guided path** designed in #20. Every battle opens with a short warm-up, the map gets a required main path and two branches, the academy becomes the library, and bounties gain new tags and a refresher slot. The battles themselves don't change.

This issue is the parent spec. Each ticket below is meant to become its own issue and PR.

## Source of truth

- [Guided path](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/campaign.md#guided-path): the warm-up flow, the map shape, and what's required.
- [Battle outline, Region 1](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/campaign.md#battle-outline-by-region): warm-up ideas and tags.
- [Warm-up content rules](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/playbook.md#warm-up-content-rules) and [map rules](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/playbook.md#map-rules).
- [Region 1: Planned guided path](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/regions/region-01-bog-goblins.md#planned-guided-path).
- [Bounty board rules](https://github.com/avoidthekitchen/chess-rpg-gauntlet/blob/main/docs/design/systems.md#bounty-board-and-gold): refresher bounties.

## Relation to #4 and #23

#4 (shout) and #23 (siege raider) change how enemies choose moves and re-verify the battles. This spec doesn't change any battle position or AI, so most tickets can be built in parallel with them. Two overlaps:

- **T1** and #4 both edit the Map intro text in `src/scenes/Map.ts`. Whichever lands second rebases.
- The **Region 1 playtest** waits for #4, #23 and this spec, so it tests the final shout, raider and warm-ups together.

## Decided: Grandmaster losses on the main path

**Grandmaster losses on the main path.** On Grandmaster, losing a battle you haven't cleared removes it from the map (`lostForGood`, `src/game/economy.ts:94`). Today that's fine, because the map has two routes. With a required main path, losing Mossbridge would block the Region.

**Decided by the owner (2026-10-23):** a battle that's gone still opens the battles after it, but its win doesn't count. The boss still needs 4 wins, so on Grandmaster one loss is your whole margin, as it is today. T1 adds a decision-log row for it.

## Tickets

Each ticket is its own issue (a sub-issue of this one) and its own PR. The full text lives in the ticket; this table is the index.

| | Issue | Ticket | Blocked by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T6a | #25 | Display support for the new bounty tags | — |
| T1 | #26 | Rewire the Region 1 map to a main path and branches | — |
| T2 | #27 | Warm-up data model and Region 1 warm-up content | — |
| T6b | #28 | Keep warm-up puzzles out of the bounty packs | T2 |
| T3 | #29 | The warm-up flow in the battle node | T2, T6a |
| T4 | #30 | Cut the in-battle lesson panel to a one-line reminder | T2 |
| T5 | #31 | The academy becomes the library, and Grubnak gets a boss practice | T3 |
| T7 | #32 | Theme tracking and refresher bounties | T2, T6a, T6b |
| T8 | #33 | Docs as built, then the playtest | All of the above, #4, #23 |

## Order

1. **T6a** (#25), **T1** (#26) and **T2** (#27) can start now, in parallel.
2. **T6b** (#28) and **T4** (#30) after T2.
3. **T3** (#29) after T2 and T6a. Its warm-ups use the new tags, which the puzzle screen can only show after T6a.
4. **T5** (#31) after T3.
5. **T7** (#32) after T2, T6a and T6b.
6. **T8** (#33) last, after #4 and #23 too.

## Deferred, not in this spec

These come from #20 but don't belong in Region 1's first pass:

- **Tip cards:** Region 1 has none; build them with Region 3.
- **The library's timed review set** (Woodpecker Method).
- **The placement check:** designed with the adaptive rating (open TODO).
- **Companion call-backs to earlier warm-ups:** more useful from Region 2, where there's an earlier Region to call back to.
- **Puzzles showing the current Region's faction:** belongs to #9.

## Checks for every ticket

`npm run ci` before each PR. T1–T7 don't change battle positions or AI, so the engine playtests shouldn't rerun. If `npm run ci` decides they should, let them run.

items.title: [Bug bounty] getTransferableAmount hardcodes destination to origin chain instead of options.destination

labels.name: Bug bounty 💰
labels.description: The issue is a bug report that, if confirmed, is eligible for a reward.

items.body:
# 🐞 Bug Report

> **Edit (correction):** the first version of this report overstated the impact (it claimed a ~30x fee underestimation for AssetHub to Hydration and High severity). That was wrong: `padFee` is only used when the origin has no DryRunApi or the dry run fails, and AssetHub, Polkadot, Hydration, Astar and Bifrost all support dry run. The report below is corrected and only claims what I verified.

## 🔍 Describe the Bug

`getTransferableAmount` receives `destination` in its options, but the origin fee used to compute the transferable amount is estimated for an **origin to origin** route instead of the requested route.

In [`getTransferableAmount.ts#L21-L43`](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/b7e9a6b05fe89686412c85be70f41792acbdd223/packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/transferable-amount/getTransferableAmount.ts#L21-L43), `getOriginFeeOrThrow` does not destructure `destination` and passes the origin chain instead:

```ts
const result = await getOriginXcmFee({
  api,
  buildTx,
  origin: chain,
  destination: chain, // options.destination is ignored
  sender,
  feeAsset,
  version,
  currency: feeCurrency,
  disableFallback: false
})
```

`buildTx` still builds the real origin to destination transfer, so the transaction and the context passed to the fee estimation disagree. Inside `getOriginXcmFee` / `getOriginXcmFeeInternal`, `destination` is used for:

- `resolveFeeAsset(...)`: the Snowbridge fee asset validation only runs when the destination is an external chain, so it is skipped.
- `pickCompatibleXcmVersion(api, origin, destination, version)`: the version is negotiated between origin and origin.
- `api.getDryRunCall({ destination, ... })`: the `chain.startsWith('AssetHub') && destination === 'Ethereum'` condition that selects the `XcmPaymentApi` fee path ([PapiApi.ts#L512](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/b7e9a6b05fe89686412c85be70f41792acbdd223/packages/sdk/src/PapiApi.ts#L512), same in Dedot and PJS) can never be true here.
- `padFee(rawFee, origin, destination, 'origin')` in the paymentInfo fallback: the route multiplier is chosen for origin to origin. In practice this only matters when a dry run fails on a relay or system chain, because the chains without DryRunApi (Centrifuge, Heima, Pendulum, Peaq) get the same 1.3x multiplier either way.

Additionally, the single-asset path calls `api.findAssetInfoOrThrow(chain, currency)` without `destination` ([L90](https://github.com/paraspell/xcm-tools/blob/b7e9a6b05fe89686412c85be70f41792acbdd223/packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/transferable-amount/getTransferableAmount.ts#L90)), while the multi-asset path passes it to `resolveCurrency` (L126).

This matters because `normalizeAmountAll` uses `getTransferableAmountInternal` to resolve `amount: 'ALL'` for cross-chain transfers, and `Builder.getTransferableAmount()` is public API.

## 🧪 To Reproduce

The existing unit test documents the behaviour: `baseOptions` uses `origin: 'Astar'`, `destination: 'BifrostPolkadot'`, but the assertion expects `getOriginXcmFee` to be called with `destination: 'Astar'`.

1. In `packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/transferable-amount/getTransferableAmount.test.ts`, change the expected `destination` in `subtracts XCM fee for native asset` to `'BifrostPolkadot'`, and add `destination: 'BifrostPolkadot'` to the `expect.objectContaining` in `returns per-asset transferable amounts in input order for currency arrays`.
2. Run:
   ```sh
   pnpm --filter @paraspell/sdk-core exec vitest run src/transfer/transferable-amount/getTransferableAmount.test.ts
   ```
3. Result on current `main`:
   ```text
   × subtracts XCM fee for native asset
   × returns per-asset transferable amounts in input order for currency arrays
   -     "destination": "BifrostPolkadot",
   +     "destination": "Astar",
   Tests  2 failed | 11 passed (13)
   ```

## 🖥️ Environment

- OS: Linux
- XCM Tool: `@paraspell/sdk-core`, `main` at `b7e9a6b0`
- Node.js: v22.22.1

## 💡 Expected Behavior

`getOriginFeeOrThrow` should forward `options.destination` to `getOriginXcmFee`, and the single-asset path should pass `destination` to `findAssetInfoOrThrow`, consistent with `Builder.getOriginXcmFee()` and the multi-asset path. With that change the full `sdk-core` suite passes locally (177 files, 1347 tests).

## 📍 Additional Context

**What is and is not verified:**

- Verified: the ignored `destination` (unit test above) and the code paths listed that consume it.
- Not verified: a live, measured fee difference or a failed on-chain transfer. I did not sign or submit any transaction. The AssetHub to Ethereum `XcmPaymentApi` path is the case where I would expect the largest difference, but I have not measured it.
- Suggested severity: Low to Medium. Happy to defer to your assessment.

**Duplicates:** I searched issues and PRs for `getTransferableAmount`, `destination: chain` and `padFee`. #2176 concerns the native existential deposit being subtracted twice in `computeTransferableAmount`; it does not cover the ignored destination.

**AI disclosure:** Antigravity (Google DeepMind) helped with code analysis, running the tests and drafting this report. I reviewed it and can explain it.

---

## ✅ Contributor Eligibility

- [x] My GitHub account's commit history is at least 6 months old.
- [x] I have set an on-chain identity on the Polkadot People Chain for my AssetHub address (below) and requested a registrar judgement of at least `Reasonable` (verifiable via [Subscan](https://people-polkadot.subscan.io/account/16G1bgZQppUozXQtoPvLDSkx4WnYaVXtuBY7pC3Wp2ytLmLy)).
- [x] I disclose any AI tools used to help write this report (or confirm none were used), and I understand and can explain its contents myself.
- [x] This report was authored and submitted by a human, not opened autonomously by an AI agent.
